fields.sample_size: Single-city case study (Lima): fieldtrip March to June 2009 combining a review of policy documents and archives (the utility SEDAPAL, the regulator SUNASS and the National Library), regular visits to peripheral communities, attendance at public events on water services and interviews with local residents, regulators, policy-makers and representatives of multilateral agencies; the number of interviews is not reported
fields.effect_measure: qualitative case study (documents, field visits, interviews); no quantitative estimate
fields.effect_estimate: Water reform in Lima was neoliberalised in two phases: the 1990s attempt to privatise the national utility SEDAPAL, definitively cancelled in 1997 (interviewees pointed to the certainty of much higher tariffs and the state's continuing investment burden), and the 2000s public-private partnerships and flexible mechanisms, which the public accepted more easily. More than three billion dollars were invested in 20 years, largely financed by higher tariffs and foreign loans, yet the reforms did not address the discriminatory treatment of low-income residents, the chaotic expansion of the metropolitan area or the risk of future shortage: in 2007 8.5% of the population still depended on water lorries, 3.9% on public fountains and 4.3% on boreholes or watercourses, and around 43% of residents lived in illegal or semi-illegal dwellings with restricted access to public water services.
fields.section: Full text (author's final draft, about 30 pages including references): 1. Introduction; 2. Water management and the neoliberalisation of nature; 3. Aims, achievements and limits of the neoliberalisation of water in Lima (3.1-3.2); 4. Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Introduction (service statistics, 2007 access data; fieldwork paragraph); section 3 (reforms of the 1990s and 2000s); Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative single-city case study of Lima's water reforms (1990s and 2000s) based on a 2009 fieldtrip (documents, visits, interviews); no quantitative estimate; read in full text 2026-10-09.
